findings.evidenceJa: それは、赤い海にいた
findings.governingReading: The unnamed subject is in a red sea.
findings.explanation: mirror moon leaves the opening page blank, omitting the impersonal subject, red sea, and initial situation.

findings.highlight: turning the town into an aquarium
findings.evidenceJa: 街は生け簀のようだった
findings.governingReading: The submerged city resembles an ikesu, a tank in which live fish are confined or kept.
findings.explanation: The English changes the predatory confinement image into a display aquarium.

findings.highlight: something thick flows into the throat
findings.evidenceJa: 濃いものが喉にからみつく
findings.governingReading: With every breath, a dense substance coils around or clings to the throat.
findings.explanation: The English changes constricting contact into simple inward flow.

findings.evidenceJa: 海中である事に間違いはないようだった
findings.governingReading: The heavy air and suffocation make it seem to the perceiver that this must be underwater.
findings.explanation: The English strengthens a subjective appearance into categorical necessity.

findings.highlight: It gasps out that it is painful
findings.evidenceJa: 苦しい、とそれは喘いだ
findings.governingReading: The subject gasps that it is suffering or cannot breathe.
findings.explanation: The English calls the sensation pain, breaking the ensuing contrast that there is no pain.

findings.evidenceJa: 本来地上に棲むべきもの
findings.governingReading: The subject is a creature that by its nature ought to live on land.
findings.explanation: The English changes normative biological incompatibility into a statement about prior residence.

findings.highlight: lungs burning from lack of oxygen
findings.evidenceJa: 足りない酸素に喉を焼き
findings.governingReading: Insufficient oxygen burns the subject’s throat.
findings.explanation: The English moves the sensation to the lungs.

findings.evidenceJa: 安穏と眠る街並を憎悪した
findings.governingReading: Its suffering makes it hate the peacefully sleeping cityscape below.
findings.explanation: The English changes hatred into a curse and the target from the cityscape to its people.

findings.highlight: It hurts. It hurts. It hurts. It hurts
findings.evidenceJa: クルシイ。クルシイ。クルシイ。クルシイ
findings.governingReading: The repeated cry is “suffering,” “suffocating,” or “distressing,” explicitly distinct from pain.
findings.explanation: The English repeatedly calls it hurt, directly contradicting the active line “There’s no pain here.”

findings.highlight: Its body is dyed bright red
findings.evidenceJa: 見惚れるほどに滑らかに彩られていた
findings.governingReading: The body is colored with a smoothness entrancing enough to gaze at.
findings.explanation: The English removes the eerie smooth beauty and adds the specific color bright red.

findings.evidenceJa: タリナイ。タリナイ。タリナイ。タリナイ
findings.governingReading: The dream repeats “Not enough” four times as distress turns into hunger.
findings.explanation: The English omits the full page and the structural transition from suffering to insufficiency.

findings.highlight: It smashes them, dyeing itself red
findings.evidenceJa: ぐちゃりと鳴るごとに、全身を濡らしていく
findings.governingReading: Each wet crushing sound is accompanied by liquid soaking the subject’s entire body.
findings.explanation: The English invents a direct object, completed smashing, and red dyeing.

findings.evidenceJa: 酸素が苦しい
findings.governingReading: The lack or condition of oxygen is distressing and suffocating.
findings.explanation: The English changes oxygen to air and again converts distress into pain.

findings.evidenceJa: 水圧が軽々しい
findings.governingReading: The dream paradoxically characterizes the water pressure as light, trivial, or insubstantial before saying it is unbearable.
findings.explanation: The English personifies the pressure as indifferent and loses the contradiction in physical weight.

findings.highlight: the only watertight protection it has
findings.evidenceJa: 耐水服だと信じるように
findings.governingReading: The subject smears itself with liquid as though believing it to be protective clothing for surviving the deep sea.
findings.explanation: The English changes clothing into generic protection and calls it watertight.

findings.evidenceJa: 街の一部分を押し潰そう
findings.governingReading: The giant shadow-hand descends as if to crush one part of the city.
findings.explanation: The English broadens the intended target to the entire town.

findings.evidenceJa: 濃い紅に塗れていた
findings.governingReading: On waking, her hands appear coated in deep crimson, which she soon recognizes as an illusion.
findings.explanation: The English immediately identifies the substance as blood rather than preserving the initial visual perception.

findings.highlight: All the parts in her body will spill out like that
findings.evidenceJa: いつか空っぽになって動かなくなる
findings.governingReading: She imagines gracelessly spilling her internal parts until she is empty and no longer moves.
findings.explanation: The English preserves spilling parts but omits the feared endpoint of emptiness and immobility.

findings.highlight: the parts in her body will spill out
findings.evidenceJa: 無様に中身をこぼしていって
findings.governingReading: She imagines the contents spilling out of her in a wretched, graceless manner.
findings.explanation: The English removes her self-disgust at the imagined spectacle.

findings.highlight: She makes it only a few steps
findings.evidenceJa: 数歩も歩けない
findings.governingReading: She cannot walk even a few steps toward the washroom.
findings.explanation: The English asserts that she does complete several steps.

findings.highlight: She braces herself against a desk
findings.evidenceJa: 倒れようとする体を、なんとか机によりかかって持ち堪えた
findings.governingReading: She barely keeps her collapsing body upright by leaning against the desk.
findings.explanation: The English removes imminent collapse and the effort required to withstand it.

findings.evidenceJa: 欲望と飢え
findings.governingReading: When memory and thought fail, only desire and hunger remain.
findings.explanation: The English moralizes desire as greed.

findings.evidenceJa: 熱い身体
findings.governingReading: She longs for a warm or hot body and gentle words.
findings.explanation: The English narrows the whole embodied warmth to skin.

findings.evidenceJa: 自分はどうかしている
findings.governingReading: She first thinks something is wrong, then repeats more personally that she herself is wrong or deranged.
findings.explanation: The English omits the self-directed repetition.

findings.evidenceJa: とてもとても空っぽ
findings.governingReading: She concludes she must be profoundly, doubly empty.
findings.explanation: The English removes the emphatic degree.

findings.evidenceJa: 彼以外の人間になんて満たしてほしくもなかった
findings.governingReading: She does not want anyone other than Shirou to fill the emptiness in her.
findings.explanation: The English removes the crucial filling relation and sounds like general social exclusivity.

findings.highlight: She wants to be his for much longer
findings.evidenceJa: いつまでもあのまま彼のものになっていたかった
findings.governingReading: She wants to remain his, in that state, forever.
findings.explanation: The English reduces indefinite permanence to a longer duration and omits continuity of the state.

findings.highlight: at the cost of time, emotion, and other people
findings.evidenceJa: 時間も感情も他の人間も何もかもなくなってしまえばいい
findings.governingReading: She wishes time, feelings, other people, and everything else would cease to exist.
findings.explanation: The English reframes annihilation as costs paid for the desired state.

findings.evidenceJa: おかしな妄想にではない
findings.governingReading: Her dizziness is not caused merely by having the bizarre fantasy.
findings.explanation: The English instead judges that the fantasy is plausible.

findings.highlight: She really thought that it would be fun
findings.evidenceJa: 一瞬、本当に素直に、それは楽しそうだな
findings.governingReading: For one instant she sincerely and unguardedly thinks the destructive prospect sounds enjoyable.
findings.explanation: The English removes the fleeting instant and the frightening absence of inner resistance.

findings.evidenceJa: 心までおかしくなり始めている
findings.governingReading: She fears that deterioration, previously bodily, is now beginning to affect her mind as well.
findings.explanation: The English escalates early mental abnormality into madness.

findings.evidenceJa: かみ締めた唇から、くぐもった嗚咽が漏れる
findings.governingReading: Muffled sobs escape through Sakura’s tightly bitten lips.
findings.explanation: The English changes sobbing into moaning and removes both muffling and the bitten-lip restraint.

findings.evidenceJa: 手足がきかなくなって、一生寝たきり
findings.governingReading: She says even losing use of her limbs and remaining bedridden for life would not frighten her.
findings.explanation: The English retains lifelong bed confinement but omits the bodily disability.

findings.evidenceJa: 彼を一番苦しめる存在
findings.governingReading: She fears becoming the being who causes Shirou the greatest suffering.
findings.explanation: The English weakens profound suffering to inconvenience or trouble.

findings.evidenceJa: この故障
findings.governingReading: She cannot disclose this malfunction or breakdown in herself.
findings.explanation: The English uses the misspelling “disfunction.”

findings.evidenceJa: この場所で、あの人に笑いかけていたかった
findings.governingReading: She wants to remain in this warm place and keep smiling at him.
findings.explanation: The English removes the place whose loss motivates her refusal to disclose the breakdown.

findings.highlight: She wishes for one person’s happiness
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女が幸せになってほしいと願うただ一人の人間
findings.governingReading: Her happiness would require ruining the one person who wishes for her to be happy.
findings.explanation: The English reverses who wishes for whose happiness, assigning the wish to Sakura.

findings.highlight: she should just break down and disappear
findings.evidenceJa: 誰にも知られないうちに壊れていなくなってしまえばいい
findings.governingReading: She imagines breaking down and disappearing before anyone learns what is happening.
findings.explanation: The English omits concealment before discovery, central to her refusal to ask for help.

findings.evidenceJa: 一番正しい選択
findings.governingReading: She calls solitary disappearance the most morally correct choice.
findings.explanation: The English changes moral rightness into unspecified optimality.

findings.evidenceJa: どうして自分だけが
findings.governingReading: Sakura asks why she alone must be cut off from an ordinary desire.
findings.explanation: The English removes the isolating “only me” focus.

findings.evidenceJa: 断絶されていなければならない
findings.governingReading: She asks why she must remain severed from ordinary warmth and happiness.
findings.explanation: The English changes existential deprivation into an external prohibition.

findings.evidenceJa: もう少し赦されていたい
findings.governingReading: In self-justification, Sakura says she only wants to be allowed or forgiven to remain a little longer.
findings.explanation: The English drops both permission/forgiveness and the limited additional time.

findings.evidenceJa: 弁解する
findings.governingReading: Sakura makes excuses or pleads a defense against recognizing envy and resentment.
findings.explanation: The English invents a settled decision for her to justify.

findings.evidenceJa: この道に、幸福な出口などない
findings.governingReading: She looks away from the obvious conclusion that this particular path offers no happy exit.
findings.explanation: The English universalizes a path-specific judgment into a claim that no happy endings exist.

findings.evidenceJa: とうに悪夢に落ちている
findings.governingReading: Her muddied thought has long since fallen into nightmare.
findings.explanation: The English adds a separate additional nightmare and weakens the metaphor of cognition descending into it.
